title: Kubernetes deploys
description: Adds deploy/dev.yaml, staging.yaml and production.yaml, each environment's values, and the deploy task: it ships the image of the data model to the cluster (loaded into a local one, pushed for any other), writes the release's Secret from an env file, upgrades the release with rollback on failure and runs helm test, with --chart-only to keep the image that runs. The chart:e2e task installs every component on a throwaway kind cluster against an in-memory DuckDB. kubectl and kind are pinned in mise.toml.

context_before: - A metric that a dashboard or an application depends on gets a golden query in `tests/queries`, with absolute date ranges.

- A change to the Helm chart in `charts/cube` comes with its unit tests in `charts/cube/tests` and a version bump in `Chart.yaml`. Each value is documented by the `# --` comment above it in `values.yaml`, which `mise run chart:docs` turns into the chart's README, and validated by `values.schema.json`.
added: - Deployments go through `mise run deploy` or the deploy workflow, never a hand-run `helm upgrade`, so that each release is a commit and an image of its data model, and rolls back by itself when a new pod cannot start.

context_before: `charts/cube` runs Cube in production on Kubernetes: the API instances behind a Service, the refresh worker and a Cube Store cluster, as non-root pods that drain on shutdown and take no traffic until they have compiled the model. [Its README](charts/cube/README.md) explains its design and lists its values. Before a pull request that changes it, `mise run chart:lint` lints it and validates what it renders for every environment, and `mise run chart:test` runs its unit tests; `mise run check` runs both before the data model check. After a change to `values.yaml`, `mise run chart:docs` regenerates its README.
added: `mise run deploy [environment]` deploys the chart with the values of `deploy/<environment>.yaml`, `dev` by default, to the current kubectl context:

1. It builds the image of the data model with `mise run image`, and loads it into a cluster on this machine (kind, minikube, Docker Desktop, OrbStack) or pushes it to the registry for any other. An unchanged model keeps its image, so its pods do not restart.

-env` from an env file of `CUBEJS_*` variables, `CUBEJS_API_SECRET` and the data source credentials: `.env` for dev, the file `CUBE_ENV_FILE` names otherwise. Without one, a Secret managed elsewhere, by External Secrets for example, stays as it is.
3. It upgrades the release, which rolls back by itself when a new pod cannot start, as when the model does not compile or the data source is out of reach, then runs `helm test`.
`mise run deploy dev --chart-only` deploys a change to the chart or its values and keeps the image that runs. Staging and production deploy committed work only, and `helm history
` lists each release with the commit it deployed, which `helm rollback` returns to. `mise run chart:e2e` installs everything on a throwaway kind cluster.

Before the first staging or production deploy, give Cube Store a bucket of its own in `deploy/<environment>.yaml`, since the volume it uses by default suits a single node, and let the cluster pull from the image's registry, with `imagePullSecrets` if it is private.
# Deploys: kubectl, and kind for the chart:e2e task.

content: # Values for mise run chart:e2e: the whole topology, small enough for a one-node
# kind cluster, on an in-memory DuckDB so it needs no data source.
# Values of the chart for a development cluster on this machine (kind,
# minikube, Docker Desktop, OrbStack): one small replica of everything, and
# Cube Store on a local volume. mise run deploy dev reads it.
# mise run deploy fills it from .env.
# Values of the chart for production, deployed once staging has the same
# commit and the production environment's reviewers approve it.
# Cube drops tables it does not know from this schema: never share it with
# The deploy workflow fills it from the production environment's CUBE_ENV
# secret; mise run deploy does from CUBE_ENV_FILE.
# Before the first deploy, move Cube Store to a bucket of its own, which
# every node reaches from any Kubernetes node, for example:
# Values of the chart for staging, deployed on every push to main. Size it like
# production, at a smaller scale, so staging catches what production would hit.
# Cube drops tables it does not know from this schema: never share it with
# The deploy workflow fills it from the staging environment's CUBE_ENV
# secret; mise run deploy does from CUBE_ENV_FILE.
# Before the first deploy, move Cube Store to a bucket of its own, which
# every node reaches from any Kubernetes node, for example:
#MISE description="Install the chart with the data model on a throwaway kind cluster and run its tests"
-e2e, loads the image the image task
# component, on an in-memory DuckDB) and runs helm test. The cluster is deleted
# afterwards unless --keep is given; a kept cluster is reused by the next run.
if ! kind get clusters 2>/dev/null | grep -qx "$cluster"; then
kubectl --context "$context" --namespace e2e get pods,pvc --output wide || true
kubectl --context "$context" --namespace e2e get events --sort-by .lastTimestamp | tail -n 30 || true
#MISE description="Deploy Cube and the data model to a Kubernetes environment: deploy [ENVIRONMENT] [--chart-only]"
# Deploys charts/cube with the values of deploy/ENVIRONMENT.yaml (default: dev)
# to the current kubectl context, in three steps:
#  1. The image task builds the image that holds the data model. A cluster on
#     this machine (kind, minikube, Docker Desktop, OrbStack, Rancher Desktop)
#     gets it loaded; any other pulls it from the registry it is pushed to.
#     --chart-only skips the image and keeps the one the release runs, for a
#     change to the chart or its values alone.
#  2. The Secret <release>-env gets the CUBEJS_* variables of an env file:
#     CUBE_ENV_FILE, or .env for dev. Without one, a Secret managed elsewhere
#     stays as it is. When the file sets no CUBEJS_API_SECRET, the Secret keeps
#     the one it has, or gets a new one.
#  3. helm upgrade --install rolls the release back if it fails, then helm test
#     checks that the API reaches the data source and that the model compiles.
# Staging and production deploy committed work only. Settings: KUBE_CONTEXT,
# the image task), CUBE_ENV_FILE and CUBE_DEPLOY_TIMEOUT (default 10m).
[ -f "$values" ] || die "no $values; the environments are: $(ls deploy | sed 's/\.yaml$//' | tr '\n' ' ')"
[ "$environment" = dev ] || die "$environment deploys committed work only; commit or stash your changes first"
# One image per architecture for Cube Store: take this machine's.
die "dev reads the data source connection from .env: copy .env.example to .env and fill it in"
# Rolls the pods when the Secret's content changed.
die "no Secret $secret yet: give its CUBEJS_* variables in an env file, CUBE_ENV_FILE=path mise run deploy $environment"
if [ "$environment" != dev ] && helm template "$release" charts/cube "$@" | grep -q CUBESTORE_REMOTE_DIR; then
echo "warning: Cube Store keeps its data on a volume in $values; give it an s3 or gcs bucket for production" >&2
echo "The release runs Cube without a data model yet; mise run deploy $environment builds and deploys it." >&2

hooks.label: Install the Helm chart in the current Kubernetes context
hooks.description: Runs `mise run deploy dev --chart-only` once the scaffold is committed, and again when weft update changes the chart or deploy/dev.yaml: installs or upgrades the release (API instances, refresh worker, Cube Store) and keeps the image it runs, Cube's own until the data model is deployed. Gated on deploy_kubernetes.

hooks.label: Deploy the data model to the current Kubernetes context
hooks.description: Runs `mise run deploy dev` after deploy-helm, and again when weft update changes cube/ or the Dockerfile: builds the image of the data model, loads or pushes it, rolls the release onto it and runs helm test. Gated on deploy_kubernetes.
